lemma: Let L = ceil(log2(n+s)) and m = s(2L+2)+L. If m < 2^n, then some Boolean function on n inputs has circuit size > s over {AND, OR, XOR, NOT} (NOT counted as a gate). Proof: a circuit of size <= s is determined by an m-bit description (per gate: 2-bit op code and two operand indices of L bits each, plus an L-bit output index). The map from descriptions to truth tables therefore has image of size <= 2^m. There are 2^(2^n) n-variable functions, and 2^m < 2^(2^n) when m < 2^n, so by pigeonhole some function is not in the image. Folklore counting; not a new theorem.
